Question 1
?

Let a=−2i−2j+4k and b=2i−2j. Find the vector projection of a onto b.

a
⟨34,−34,0⟩
b
⟨0,0,0⟩
c
⟨6,−6,0⟩
d
⟨−32,32,0⟩
e
0
Submit

decision.explanation: The vector projection is (a·b)/(b·b) times b. Since a·b=(-2)(2)+(-2)(-2)+4(0)=0 and b·b=8, the projection is ⟨0,0,0⟩.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Let $a=-2i-2j+4k$ and $b=2i-2j.$ Find the vector projection of $a$ onto $b.$
after.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{(-2)\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-2)+4\cdot 0}{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{0}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{0}{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{0}^{2}}b \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Let $a=-2i-2j+4k$ and $b=2i-2j.$ Find the vector projection of $a$ onto $b.$
content.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{(-2)\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-2)+4\cdot 0}{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{0}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{0}{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{0}^{2}}b \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ x\end{aligned}].$ Given that the projection of $a$ onto $b$ is the zero vector, find the value of $x.$
after.worked_solution:
Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =-4\cdot 4+4\cdot (-1)+1\cdot x \\  & =x-20.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ x-20 & =0 \\ x & =20.\end{aligned}
$$
